links.targetTitle: The Aave revenue-share clock stops when Spark's activity fal

title: Before SPK launched, Aave's revenue share was paid on assumed income rather than actual income
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.2.3.1 constructs a synthetic basis for a real payment. Before Agent tokens existed, "Sky Governance is temporarily responsible for paying out a 'virtual revenue share' on behalf of Spark Protocol. It is calculated by taking the total amount of Dai borrowed from Spark Protocol, and then **assuming** a 'virtual income' equivalent to 1% of this supply, and calculating a revenue share of 10% on that basis." The worked example: 200 million Dai borrowed → 2 million virtual income → 200,000 Dai owed.

The device solves a real accounting problem. Spark's Dai market is priced administratively as a spread over the Sky Savings Rate, and pre-launch Spark had no token, no treasury of its own, and no clean separation of its income from Sky's. Measuring "Spark's income from Aave-derived functionality" in that period would have been contestable in every direction.

Substituting a formula removes the dispute entirely. Both sides can compute the number from a single public quantity — Dai borrowed — with no access to books and no room for interpretation. The 1% is not an estimate anyone must defend as accurate; it is a convention agreed in advance, which is a different and much cheaper thing to agree on.

The cost is that the payer is not the beneficiary: Sky Governance pays from the Sky Surplus Buffer to a contract controlled by Aave Governance, on behalf of a Spark that has not yet been separated out. And the whole thing runs on manual quarterly calculation by the Support Facilitators — an obligation of hundreds of thousands of Dai with a human process and no automation behind it.
description: Sky Governance paid a 'virtual revenue share' computed as 10% of a virtual income defined as 1% of Dai borrowed from Spark, discharging the obligation without measuring real revenue.
